title: Acts Not Constituting Infringement of Copyright (Fair Dealing)
content:
Section 52 of the Copyright Act, 1957 specifies acts that do not constitute an infringement of copyright. Under Section 52(1)(a), fair dealing with any work for private or personal use (including research), criticism, review, or reporting of current events does not infringe copyright. Section 52(1)(q) permits the reproduction or publication of any matter published in any Official Gazette or reports of government committees.

Key Legal Implications for Ayurvedic Research & Prior Art Scrutiny:
1. Patent examiners, researchers, and AYUSH scientists who cite, excerpt, or analyze copyrighted modern botanical papers, clinical trial results, or pharmacognosy texts for verifying prior art or non-obviousness are protected under fair dealing.
2. Government pharmacopoeial monographs (e.g., Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India) published under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act can be referenced and cited freely for statutory compliance.
